questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I could understand the native language and therefore more easily immerse myself in the culture.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: Overall okay. The host institution didn't register me correctly to begin with but it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always phone someone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Call people. It's easier to sort it out that way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would have liked to take master courses as the courses I took were a bit boring academically.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Sometimes more on hands teachers like you would find in Danish high schools.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
The Labour Party & Socialism
Political Transition in the Middle East: A Century of Conflict
Africa & International Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Plenty of options but the UK specific one was the best.

questions.answer: A lot. Only participated in some more academic clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Some student activities might be more social than the classes. However, the students are younger in England than in Denmark so I mostly spent time with the PhD students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go traveling. York is the local hub for the railway network so getting to the rest of the England and Scotland is easy and pretty cheap with a railcard.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty. Speaking the language is a godsend.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals are very friendly and welcoming. Going into a pub and striking up a conversation is easy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Yorkshire is very friendly and easy to adapt to
York is a good spot to explore the rest of England and Scotland from
The colleges aren't very social and no kitchen stuff is shared
